hud-bench-start: Komet HUD: benchmark running for {0} s
hud-bench-done: Komet HUD: benchmark done, results copied to clipboard and client log
cmd-hud-open-failed: Komet HUD: settings window could not be opened
hud-update-mismatch: Up to date, but your file differs ({0})
hud-update-unverified: Up to date, no checksum to compare
hud-update-norelease: {0} is not on GitHub, nothing to compare
update-ask: Should Komet look for updates when the game starts? It also checks that your installed file is exactly the published one. This sends one request to GitHub (api.github.com) each start. You can change this any time in the Komet settings.
settings-checksum-hint: Shows your version, the newest one on GitHub, and whether your installed file is exactly the published one.
verify-match: Your file is exactly the one published for {0}.
verify-mismatch: Your file is NOT the one published for {0}. Best download Komet again from GitHub.
verify-norelease: {0} is not on GitHub, so there is nothing to compare.
verify-prebuild: {0} is a pre-release for testing and not published on GitHub yet. Komet tells you once a newer version is out.
verify-nofile: Komet was loaded from a folder, there is no file to check.
hud-spikes: Spikes over {0} ms or {1}× average, by cause
hud-spike-line: {0} s: {1} ms, {2} | GC {3} ms, between frames {4} ms, JIT {5} ms, waiting for a core {6} ms | marks: {7}
settings-updates-hint: Looks for a newer Komet version on GitHub each time you join a world and checks that your file is unchanged. This sends one request to api.github.com.
settings-showadvanced-hint: Shows every Komet switch, including the hidden ones. They give the same result as the game (or fix a bug in it), just faster or leaner, and stay on. Only turn one off to track down a problem.
settings-rebuild-hint: Rebuilds all loaded chunks without leaving the world and frees their video memory. Switches like save video memory take effect at once. The terrain is back after a few seconds.
settings-hardware: This computer: {0} cores, {1} GB RAM, {2} GB video memory, {3} Hz
settings-detected-hint: Resets every option you changed on these pages to the preset and to what suits this computer (based on RAM, video memory and monitor). HUD and tool settings stay.
settings-exact-area-hint: Every exact switch of this area at once.
settings-exact-about: Each one gives the same picture and the same game as without Komet, only faster or leaner. Leave them on; turn one off only to track down a problem.
settings-exact-all-hint: Every switch below at once. Each gives the same result as the game (or fixes a bug in it), just faster or leaner. Only turn one off to track down a problem, and name it in your bug report.
settings-preset-hint: Sets view distance, shadows, effects, particles and resolution in one go. If you change one of them afterwards, the preset shows Custom.
settings-komet-preset-hint: Sets the options on the Rendering, Chunks, Other and Vulkan pages at once. Automatic: Balanced, or Speed on a weak computer. What you change yourself stays, and the preset shows Adjusted. Settings for your computer still apply.
settings-shaders-none: No shader packs or shader mods active
settings-shaders-folder-hint: Put a folder with a komet-shader.json here to try a pack without a mod of your own. A ready example is under Modding › Templates, the guide under Modding › Shader reference.
settings-shaders-reload-hint: Reads every shader pack and shader mod again: komet.json, shaders, includes and Komet versions. Changes show at once, without leaving the world. Errors go to the client log.
settings-add-mod-template-hint: Puts a small, working shader mod made for Komet into {0} and opens the folder: modinfo.json, komet.json with a switch and a slider and a picture effect. Copy the folder into your Mods folder and make it your own. Guide: Modding › Your mod for Komet.
settings-add-vulkan-template-hint: Puts a complete shader package for developers into {0} and opens the folder: two passes (depth haze, colour grading), sliders, a define, texts in two languages, the rules for Vulkan and an optional C# part. Runs on OpenGL and on Komet's Vulkan renderer. Guide: Modding › Shaders on Vulkan and the README.md in the folder.
settings-add-example-pack-hint: Puts a small shader pack into {0}: a komet-shader.json with a switch, a slider and a shader file that tints the picture. It shows up at once as its own page under Shaders. Read it, change it, copy it. Guide: Modding › Shader reference.
settings-templates-own: Without a mod of your own
settings-templates-folder-hint: The mod template and the Vulkan template put their folders here: {0}. A template does nothing until you copy its folder into the Mods folder.
settings-mods-folder-hint: The folder the game loads your mods from: {0}. Copy a template here and join the world again.
settings-shaders-found-files: Replaces {0} shaders and {1} include files of the game and brings {2} shaders of its own.
settings-shaders-found-unloaded: Its shaders are not loaded yet.
settings-shaders-found-gl: {0} of {1} shaders do not compile under OpenGL: {2}. The errors are in client-main.log.
settings-shaders-found-vulkan: {0} of {1} shaders cannot be translated for Vulkan, for example {2}: {3}
settings-shaders-found-porting: Komet is translating {0} of {1} shaders for Vulkan.
settings-shaders-found-vulkan-ok: All {0} shaders are translated for Vulkan.
settings-shaders-found-held: Off right now: Komet holds the mod back, its systems do not run and the game uses its own shaders. Switching it on starts it at once.
settings-adapter-level-hint: "As Komet" follows Komet's preset: Quality takes {0}'s own default profile, Speed its performance profile. "Own" leaves {0}'s settings alone; its own window applies then.
settings-shaders-found-variants: Brings {0} shader files tuned for Komet, which Komet uses instead of the normal ones.
settings-shaders-bound-speaks: Talks to Komet: the mod announces itself and tells Komet what it needs.
settings-shaders-bound-takesover: Komet takes over: the mod knows nothing of Komet; Komet steers it through a binding it ships.
settings-shaders-bound-found: Detected only: Komet knows the mod by its files but does not steer it.
settings-shaders-found-opengl: Draws with OpenGL only: while the mod runs, Komet takes OpenGL instead of Vulkan.
settings-fact-speaks-json: Talks to Komet itself through its komet.json
settings-fact-speaks-code: Talks to Komet itself through the code API
settings-fact-speaks-pack: Talks to Komet as a pack from your folder
settings-fact-takesover: Komet takes over: the mod knows nothing of Komet; Komet steers it through a binding it ships
settings-fact-found: Detected only: Komet knows its files but does not steer it
settings-fact-gl-only: Runs on OpenGL, as the mod draws with OpenGL only
settings-fact-vk-ok: Runs on Vulkan, all {0} shaders translated
settings-fact-vk-porting: Runs on Vulkan, {0} of {1} shaders being translated
settings-fact-vk-partial: Runs on Vulkan, {0} of {1} shaders not translated (for example {2})
settings-fact-shaders-none: Its shaders are not loaded yet
settings-fact-variants: Brings {0} Komet versions of its files
settings-fact-held: Held back: not running now; the game uses its own files
settings-shaders-found-paused: {0} is paused: the game draws with its own shaders again.
settings-shaders-found-next: Switched off: the mod keeps running until you next enter a world; a running mod cannot be stopped safely.
settings-shaders-found-missing: Needs the mod {0} ({1}), which is not installed.
settings-shaders-found-version: Was built for {0} {1}, {2} is loaded. Komet does not start it, as the game would crash. Install a matching version.
hud-shaders-held: Komet: these shader mods are off until you switch them on (Shaders › Active shaders): {0}
settings-shaders-others-join: A komet.json makes it Komet-compatible (Modding › Your mod for Komet).
settings-original-hint: Opens the game's settings menu as it looks without Komet.
settings-key-hint: Click, then press a key, key combination or mouse button. Escape keeps the old binding, × removes it, a right click restores the game's default.
settings-reset-hint: Click twice: the first click only asks.
settings-slider-keys: ← → one step · Shift: ten steps · Home / End · Tab: next slider
settings-graphicsmenu-hint: Shows this menu instead of the game's settings. Off: the game's own menu. The chat command .komet always opens it.
settings-menublur-hint: Blurs the world and HUD behind this menu. Off: only darkened.
settings-held: Another mod needs the game's own behaviour here. Once it lets go, your choice applies again.
settings-shaderusecache-hint: Sends only changed shader values to the GPU instead of all of them every time.
settings-distantshadows-hint: Terrain casts shadows up to your view distance instead of only about 200 blocks. Far shadows are redrawn bit by bit, only when the sun moves or you travel far, so they cost little. Near shadows stay as in the game.
settings-occlusionculling-hint: The GPU leaves out terrain you can't see. 0: as in the game. 1: also terrain hidden behind other terrain. 2: the GPU does it all and takes load off the CPU. Vulkan only; if your GPU can't do 2, 1 applies.
settings-vulkan-advanced: Advanced: each part on its own
settings-vulkanonlylean-hint: Vulkan renderer only. OpenGL gets no second copy of the world's large textures and data: saves uploads and usually several hundred MB of video memory. After a GPU error you must rejoin the world. Switching works best before joining a world.
settings-vulkanframebridge-hint: Experimental, Vulkan only. If a frame isn't ready in time for your monitor, Komet shows the last frame turned to match the camera. Looking around stays smooth; creatures and walking move only at the game's FPS. Costs a little GPU time.
settings-vulkanquietuniforms-hint: Vulkan only. Komet keeps the shader values the game sets every frame instead of also sending them to the unused OpenGL. Saves about 0.15 ms per frame.
settings-vulkan-mode-hint: OpenGL: the game's own renderer. Vulkan (experimental): Vulkan draws everything alone; what Vulkan can't draw is missing from the picture, and on an error OpenGL takes over again. Takes effect at once.
settings-vulkanpacing-hint: Waits for the GPU at the start of each frame instead of in the middle. When the GPU is the limit, the camera moves more evenly, with fewer microstutters.
settings-vulkangputimes-hint: Measures how long the GPU takes for terrain, sky, creatures, particles and effects, and writes it to the log. Costs a little performance.
settings-vulkanshadercache-hint: Saves translated shaders to disk (VintagestoryData/Cache/komet-vulkan). From the next start, this removes most stutters when the world, creatures or particles first appear. After a Komet update they are translated again.
settings-frustumsweep-hint: Checks faster which chunks are in view, with the same result as the game. With very many chunks, more CPU cores help out.
settings-leanvaryings-hint: The terrain shaders pass on fewer values and work them out per pixel instead. This takes load off the GPU. The same picture apart from tiny rounding. Takes effect when the shaders next reload.
settings-nearshadowreuse-hint: Doesn't redraw near shadows every frame while the sun, terrain, your position and view barely change. Saves GPU time (up to 1.5 ms per frame in a forest); shadows get very slightly coarser. Below 60 FPS as in the game.
settings-farshadowreuse-hint: Redraws far shadows at most every 33 ms instead of every frame; the sun barely moves in that time. Redrawn at once if terrain or light changes or the camera jumps. Far creature shadows update at about 30 Hz.
settings-farlod-hint: Past the distance where a block covers fewer than this many pixels, chunks are built coarser: a quarter of the faces, past twice that distance a sixteenth, which eases load on the GPU and video memory. Plants and decor are missing there, textures look larger. 0 turns it off.
settings-farfoliage-hint: Past the distance where a block covers fewer than this many pixels, every other leaf block is left out, and grass, flowers, ferns and crops disappear. Hardly visible at 1 pixel; distant forests have about half the faces. 0 turns it off.
settings-deepculling-hint: Chunks deep below the surface hold cave walls no one sees from above, a fifth to a third of the terrain at large view distances. Beyond 96 blocks (256 when you're underground) they aren't drawn; this saves video memory.
settings-leangodrays-hint: The god rays read the scene only in the sky, not behind the terrain. The same picture, less work for the GPU.
settings-leanpost-hint: God rays take half as many steps, the ambient occlusion (SSAO) blur 7 samples instead of 11, and particles such as raindrops read the shadow once instead of nine times a pixel. Rain then costs little frame rate; the edges of these effects get a little softer.
settings-framepacer-hint: Keeps the FPS cap exact. The game rounds to whole milliseconds, so frames alternate between short and long (microstutter). Only with VSync off and an FPS cap set.
settings-framesmoothing: Even frame times without a cap
settings-framesmoothing-hint: Without a frame rate cap, frames vary by a few milliseconds and turning feels uneven despite a high FPS. Komet then paces each frame to a little above what recent frames took. The FPS barely drops and the picture runs evenly.
settings-backgroundpriority-hint: Runs background work (world server, chunk building, light) at slightly lower priority so the frame comes first. Helps on CPUs with few threads: with 4 threads, 1 % low 18 → 23 FPS, chunks just as fast. With many threads nothing changes.
settings-gcidle-hint: Garbage collection briefly pauses the game. With an FPS cap or VSync a frame often has time to spare; Komet cleans up right there instead of in the middle of a later frame. Without spare time nothing changes.
settings-soundscratch-hint: When you join a world the game unpacks every sound. Komet sizes the memory for each one right away instead of growing and copying it several times. Less garbage collection while loading.
settings-framescratch-hint: Every frame the game creates small throwaway objects, e.g. for the hotbar, status bars, map and open windows. Komet does the same work without them. Less memory cleanup, so fewer stutters.
settings-sharpupscale-hint: Below 100 % resolution, Komet upscales the image like AMD FSR 1 instead of just stretching it. Edges stay sharp. At 100 % nothing changes.
settings-entitycasters-hint: Creatures, players and dropped items whose shadows can't reach your view are skipped when drawing shadows. Saves GPU time. The shadows look the same as without.
settings-indirectdraw-hint: Draws chunks in batches with fewer commands to the GPU. Needs an OpenGL extension (GL_ARB_multi_draw_indirect); without it, the game draws as usual.
settings-poolscale-hint: Stores chunks in fewer, larger memory blocks on the GPU. Saves draw calls. The value is the growth factor; 1 is the game's default. Takes full effect after you rejoin the world.
settings-pooltrim-hint: The game never gives back video memory for chunks, so flying leaves gigabytes unused. Level 1 frees empty space after 10 s; higher levels clean up faster and more, with more background work. 0: off.
settings-chunkpacking-hint: The game packs unused chunks late and slowly, so flying leaves thousands in RAM. Higher levels pack faster: less RAM, a bit more CPU load in the background. 0: like the game.
settings-windowsize-hint: The game asks the window system for the window size a dozen times a frame; on Linux (X11) each ask is a round trip to the display server. Komet uses the size the game already keeps and asks only when the window changes.
settings-chunklookup-hint: Answers chunk lookups from its own copy, so the game's threads don't slow each other down.
settings-animationframes-hint: Remembers computed animation frames and computes new ones faster. Whatever Komet can't do, the game handles.
settings-shapeinitmemo-hint: Skips preparing creature models again when they haven't changed.
settings-meshrecycle-hint: Reused chunk models keep their memory instead of creating it anew for every copy. Less memory cleanup.
settings-facepacking-hint: Prepares chunks for the GPU on several CPU cores instead of only the main thread. Fewer stutters while loading.
hud-modtimes: Mod CPU time per frame: renderers & tick listeners
hud-rendercost: Terrain draw cost per frame, main thread
hud-rc-nothreads: No Mesa driver threads found (Linux with Mesa only)
hud-occ-culling-off: Switched off in the render settings
hud-occ-drawn-late: Ranges drawn in the second pass
hud-pipeline: Opaque terrain in the GPU pipeline (one frame)
hud-feature-stooddown: stood down, another mod patches the same code
hud-debug-timings: Debug build – Komet's own timings are inflated roughly 2.6x
hud-cull-sorted: Pools sorted into the grid per frame
hud-cull-staged: Render calls culled with their stage
hud-anim-idle: Idle animation calls left out per frame
hud-draw-unmapped: GL_ARB_buffer_storage missing, command buffer per draw
hud-anim-fast-blocked: Another mod patches the compile, or the game changed it: engine path
hud-pool-trimmed-mb: Video memory freed from empty pools
hud-entitytimes-unpatched: The entity loops are not the ones measured: no times
hud-shapememo-blocked: Another mod patches the shape init, or the game changed it: engine path
hud-particlelight-unpatched: Patch not installed, particles wait as in the engine
hud-particlelight-reads: Light reads on the render thread per frame
hud-particlelight-packed: Chunk packed, not unpacked per frame
hud-owntess-unpatched: Not installed, the engine draws every block
hud-owntess-other: Another patch on a tessellator body, the engine draws the blocks it concerns
hud-owntess-json: Of these, simple models per frame
hud-facelight-unpatched: Patch not installed, the engine lights every face
hud-facelight-other: Another patch on the face light, the engine lights the faces it concerns
hud-facelight-blocks: JSON blocks lit in one pass per frame
hud-tess-unpatched: Counters not installed, tessellation is not measured
hud-tess-partial: A fast path did not match the game's code, the engine's version runs (see log)
hud-tess-occluded-other: Another patch on the tessellation, enclosed chunks go to the engine
hud-tess-zero: Time in chunks without a vertex
hud-tess-skipped: Empty or missing chunks per second
hud-farfoliage-unpatched: The tessellator changed, foliage is drawn in full at every distance
hud-farfoliage-thinned: Leaf blocks thinned out per second
hud-farfoliage-marked: Chunks retessellated for distance per second
hud-tess-workers-failed: Tessellation on a worker thread failed, the engine tessellates alone again (see log)
hud-tess-workers-unpatched: No tessellation on the worker threads: not every safety patch is installed
settings-partitionreuse-hint: The game rebuilds a grid for creatures from scratch 31 times a second. Komet reuses it. In large worlds this saves about 7 MB of throwaway memory a second, and so stutters.
settings-cookingmatch-hint: A firepit with a cooking pot checks all recipes several times a second and creates lots of throwaway memory. Komet reuses the memory. Same result as without.
settings-alloymatch-hint: A firepit with a crucible keeps checking all alloy recipes and creates lots of throwaway memory. Komet does without it. Same result as without.
settings-animatableculling-hint: Animated blocks like doors, chests or translocators are no longer drawn when fully out of view. Otherwise the game draws them every frame, however far away.
settings-helpcompose-hint: The interaction help (keys and items at blocks and creatures) is redrawn all the time, 5–15 ms each time. Komet redraws it only when its content changes. Fewer stutters.
settings-potculling-hint: Pots on firepits are otherwise drawn every frame, even behind you. Fully hidden pots are left out. Looks the same as without.
settings-hearthculling-hint: The contents of firepits and forges are otherwise drawn every frame, even behind you. Fully hidden ones are left out, which helps in bases with many of them. Looks the same as without.
settings-glquerycache-hint: Every frame, the clouds ask the graphics driver for its state and wait for it. Komet already knows the answer and saves the wait. Same result as without.
settings-bushshapes-hint: For each new look of a berry bush, the game reads its model file again, hundreds of times in worlds full of bushes. Komet reads each file only once. Looks the same as without.
settings-clouduploads-hint: The clouds send two textures to the graphics card up to 25 times a second, even when nothing in them changed. Komet uploads a cloud texture only when its content changed: less main-thread work, most of all at large view distances.
settings-dirtyblocks-hint: Block entities such as berry bushes catch up on growth when their chunk loads and report their block hundreds of times; the server sent one update per report. Komet sends each block once per update round. In old worlds this removes tens of thousands of packets a second while loading, and the chunk rebuilds they caused.
settings-mappixels-hint: Each piece of the world map (32 x 32 pixels) waits up to four seconds for its save, long enough for the garbage collector to move it into old memory. Komet reuses a piece once it is saved and drawn, so loading the world causes shorter collector pauses.
settings-treekeys-hint: When receiving chunks, the game makes needless text copies for each block's data. Komet avoids them. Less memory cleanup, same data as without.
settings-mappiecebudget-hint: When you join a world, the game loads up to 200 map pieces at once, which stutters at a large view distance. Komet spreads them over several frames. The map fills in over a few seconds, nothing lost.
settings-mapsavescratch-hint: Saving the world map creates about 40 MB of throwaway memory a second while chunks load, which causes stutters. Komet reuses the memory. Same data as without.
settings-maptileupload-hint: Each new map piece takes a roundabout way to the GPU, up to 200 times per tick while chunks load, which stutters. Komet uploads each piece directly. Looks the same as without.
settings-maptileculling-hint: The map and minimap draw up to a thousand tiles every frame, though only a dozen show. Komet leaves out the hidden ones. Prevents long stutters under Vulkan when you join a world.
settings-idleanimators-hint: Animated blocks (chests, doors, querns …) get updated every frame, even when standing still. Komet skips calls that would do nothing. Same result as without.
settings-climatecache-hint: Keeps climate data for every visible region in memory (up to 144) instead of only 10. Helps at large view distances, costs a little RAM.
settings-cloudtilescratch-hint: Clouds constantly make memory garbage, about 33 MB per second. Komet avoids that: fewer stutters. Works for fluffy and simple clouds.
settings-decompressscratch-hint: Unpacks arriving chunks without a throwaway copy: about 8 MB per second less memory garbage while chunks load. That means fewer stutters.
settings-directchunks-hint: In singleplayer the built-in server hands chunks, map columns and single block changes (leaves, grass, snow) to the game as they are instead of serializing, copying and reading them back. Loading makes far less garbage, and each chunk's packed data is held once.
settings-columnnoisescratch-hint: Generates new terrain with less memory garbage. Singleplayer only.
settings-neighbourreads-hint: Building a chunk only reads its neighbours, so their packed data stays and is not packed again. Fewer garbage collections hold up the game.
settings-packedchunks-hint: Chunks stay packed even when drawn or shown on the map: the tessellator and the map decode them into their own reused memory. While a world loads hardly any new chunk data is made, so garbage collection holds up the game less often. Costs a little more time on the background threads.
settings-facelight-hint: Computes the smooth light on block faces faster. Chunks are built faster.
settings-tickscratch-hint: Growing grass and barrels waiting for a recipe make memory garbage on every check of the built-in server. Komet avoids it: fewer stutters, same results.
settings-lightscratch-hint: Spreads block light with less memory garbage. That means fewer stutters.
settings-lightrepair-hint: Relighting (WorldEdit, /debug relight, the timeswitch) leaves some chunks black and puts light sources in the wrong place. Komet relights without errors and repairs those chunks for good. Singleplayer only.
settings-particlelight-hint: Particles no longer wait for chunk data and use the last light read if needed. Removes 8–13 ms stutters near beehives.
settings-relightredraws: Fewer chunk rebuilds after block changes
settings-relightredraws-hint: A block change that alters no light (snow, grass, leaves, crops) no longer rebuilds its chunk a second time. The game did that for almost every change: 30 extra chunk rebuilds a second standing still, up to 300 right after joining a world.
settings-occludedchunks-hint: A chunk fully enclosed by opaque blocks is not built at all, since you never see it. Saves processing time.
settings-tessschedule-hint: Builds the nearest chunks first, especially where you look, instead of in arrival order. Nearby chunks appear about twice as fast.
settings-workerthreads-hint: How many CPU threads Komet uses at most to build chunks. Komet decides how many work at a time (see priority). 0 = only the game's threads.
settings-tesspriority-hint: 0 % = Komet doesn't help load chunks: the smoothest frame rate. 100 % = chunks load as fast as possible, frame rate may suffer. Komet raises the share by itself when you join a world or teleport.
hud-garbage-unpatched: A rewrite did not match the game's code, the engine's version runs (see log)
hud-garbage-decompress: Chunk layer copies saved per frame
hud-garbage-noise: Terrain noise arrays saved per frame
settings-helditemslast-hint: Draws items held by creatures and players after all bodies. A glass pane in a hand no longer hides the body behind it (also a bug without mods). First person is unchanged.
settings-pointlights-hint: Light from held torches and glowing items no longer swims as you move, and weak lights glow softly instead of in patches. Fixes game bugs. Reloads the shaders.
settings-uploadcap-hint: How many milliseconds per frame chunks may be sent to the GPU. Less = fewer stutters, chunks appear slower. Important chunks may use up to 6 ms. 0 = game default, no limit.
settings-uploadyield-hint: If a frame is already slow, it sends only one chunk to the GPU and leaves the rest for the next. Chunks right around you and block changes come at once. Softens the worst stutters.
hud-uploadcap-active: Upload time cap: {0} ms per frame
hud-uploadcap-off: Upload time cap off, engine budget only
hud-uploadcap-unpatched: Upload time cap {0} ms - substitution failed, engine budget only
hud-upload-over: Frames whose chunk work went past the cap
hud-upload-over-ms: Past the cap by, per such frame
hud-upload-priority-cut: Frames that left priority chunks for the next
hud-upload-births: Chunk pools adopted as made, per second
settings-chunkloadbudget-hint: How many milliseconds per frame setting up arriving chunks may take. Far chunks otherwise wait for the next frame, nearby ones always come at once. 0 = game default, all at once.
settings-joinpacer-hint: When you join a world or explore, the built-in server sends far more chunks than the game can build, and the garbage this makes stalls the game with memory pauses. Komet slows the flow as soon as the pauses become noticeable or chunks pile up, so loading barely touches the frame rate. Near chunks still come first, far ones later. Singleplayer only.
settings-eventbussweep-hint: Ground storage, shelves, racks and firepits stayed in memory after unloading, and each new one slowed the game. Komet releases them. Behavior stays the same.
hud-chunkload-unpatched: Chunk arrival budget: substitution failed, the engine loads all at once
cmd-debug: records everything Komet measures and writes the debug protocol: [seconds|now|spike <ms>|stop] [en|de]
cmd-debug-usage: Usage: .komet debug [seconds | now | spike <ms> | stop | join] [en | de]
cmd-debug-join-on: Komet records the first minute of every world you join from now on (.komet debug join switches it off).
cmd-debug-join-off: Komet no longer records the joins.
cmd-debug-join-started: Komet records this join ({0} s); the protocol follows by itself.
cmd-debug-running: A debug capture is already running or being written.
cmd-debug-bench: The HUD benchmark is running; start the capture after it.
cmd-debug-started: Debug capture running for {0} s, every collector on.
cmd-debug-armed: Debug capture armed: the first frame over {0} ms writes the protocol. .komet debug stop ends it.
cmd-debug-stopped: Debug capture stopped, writing the protocol.
cmd-debug-done: Debug protocol copied to the clipboard and written to {0}
hud-dbg-head: {0}, {1} s, {2} frames: {3} fps, 1 % low {4} fps, worst {5} ms
hud-dbg-triggered: Triggered by a {0} ms frame at {1} s
hud-dbg-stopped: Stopped by hand before any frame crossed the threshold
hud-dbg-f-none: Nothing stands out in this capture.
hud-dbg-f-gc: The garbage collector paused the game {0} % of the time ({1} gen0 collections, longest {2} ms)
hud-dbg-f-alloc: {0} MB/s allocated, {1} % of it on the main thread
hud-dbg-f-jit: {0} ms of JIT compilation during play
hud-dbg-f-worst: A {0} ms frame: a visible hitch
hud-dbg-f-over50: {0} frames over 50 ms ({1} % of steady frames)
hud-dbg-f-runqueue: The main thread waited {0} ms per frame for a CPU (max {1} ms): other load competes
hud-dbg-f-harmony: {0} methods are patched by several mods in a way that can break one of them

settings-inventoryshapes-hint: Creature items and clothing froze the creative inventory for up to two seconds the first time you looked. Komet loads only what the icons need. Looks the same as without.
settings-snowpeek-hint: Every in-game hour the game checks all loaded chunks for snow and unpacks them to do it. At large view distances this was the biggest memory hog while flying. Komet reads them without unpacking.
settings-profilerpool-hint: The game's frame profiler, which Komet's HUD turns on, makes memory garbage every frame, about 12 % of all. Komet avoids nearly all of it.
settings-iconbudget-hint: New items take time the first time they show in the inventory, up to 150 ms for a creative inventory row. Komet draws at most 6 ms per frame, the rest appear shortly after. Icons already shown never wait.
settings-worldgenscratch-hint: In singleplayer, world generation shares memory with the game. Komet saves about 1 GB of memory garbage per minute while flying into new terrain: fewer stutters. The world comes out the same.
settings-jitwarm-hint: In a world's first seconds the game otherwise builds chunks 10 to 20 times slower, since its code isn't optimized yet. Komet optimizes it right away. Takes effect from the next world start. Looks the same as without.
settings-blockentitycaches-hint: Ground storage, firepits and pots on the fire worked out the same things over and over. Komet does it only once per kind. Results stay the same.
settings-listenerslots-hint: Without this, every chunk with block entities loads slower the longer you play. Komet keeps registering them fast. Behavior stays the same.
settings-owntessellation-hint: Komet builds simple blocks itself, faster: cubes, grassy soil, grass, plants, sand, gravel, loose stones, leaves. The game still builds everything else and blocks changed by mods. Looks the same as without.
vk-shaderc-fetching: Komet: Vulkan needs the shader compiler shaderc, which this computer does not have. Komet downloads it once ({0} MB from nuget.org); OpenGL draws meanwhile.
vk-shaderc-fetched: Komet: shaderc is downloaded. Leave the world and join it again to play with Vulkan.
vk-shaderc-failed: Komet: shaderc could not be downloaded ({0}). Vulkan stays off and OpenGL draws. Join the world again to retry, or install shaderc.
vk-shaderc-status-fetching: Vulkan waits for the shader compiler shaderc: downloading, {0} %. OpenGL draws meanwhile.
vk-shaderc-status-fetched: shaderc is downloaded: join the world again to use Vulkan.
vk-shaderc-status-failed: shaderc is missing and could not be downloaded ({0}): OpenGL draws.
settings-style-hint: How this menu looks. Pragmatic: tabs on top, page list, rows and details over a planet. Other mods and your own folders can add more styles.
settings-motion-hint: Camera moves, lists sliding in, names building up, the style change. Calm moves slower, Off moves nothing.
settings-style-folder-hint: Each subfolder with a style.json is a style: colours, fonts, sizes, logo and background shader. Location: {0}. A logo.png next to it (ModConfig/komet/logo.png) shows in the header of every style with tabs, such as Pragmatic.
settings-style-template-hint: Copies the current style with all its values into a new folder and opens it. Edit style.json and background.fsh, then reload.
settings-style-reload-hint: Reads all styles again, so changes to style.json or the shader work without a restart. Errors go to the client log.
settings-add-example-style-hint: Puts an example style with an amber accent into {0} and picks it. Open its style.json, change a colour and press Reload styles under Komet › Style. Guide: Modding › Menu styles.
shaderpack-example-tint-hint: Tints the left half of the picture red, the sky at half strength. An example of a pack switching a pass on and off.
shaderpack-example-strength-hint: How strong the red tint is. An example of a uniform that works live.
